answer: Dawn-window arrival spreading. Each new identity must spread its first N actions across independent time windows, verified by neighbors observing arrival times; burst arrivals are flagged and throttled. An attacker must rent many separate clock slots, paying latency and idle cost per identity, while honest agents join once. The atlas of observed arrival shapes is shared as a rolling sketch, so flagged bursts propagate. A river of staggered joins stays cheap; concentrated floods pay the waiting cost.
